newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: -- Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday due to a domestic A share issue on Thursday, which continued to suck funds out of the repo market, traders said.
Turnover plunged to 6.96 million lots from 13.1 million on onday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose slightly to 14.00 percent from 13.62 percent.
"The rates climbed up steadily today due to the new share issue," one trader said. "Many institutions began on Monday to borrow for the issue, so the gain today was not large."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mostly down because of weak investor confidence in returns of future treasury bonds, traders said.
But the most active three-year bond that matures in August 1999 bucked the trend and ended up at 104.00 yuan from 103.75.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 2.17 million lots from 2.81 million.
The People's Bank of China cut bank interest rates twice this year on May 1 and August 23. Traders said the cut would lead to lower coupons for T-bonds issued in the near term.
"Jitters over low returns depressed prices," said a trader.
